task.name: repeated-name-completion
task.description: Copy the continuation of a made-up two-token surname seen earlier in the context. Each prompt introduces a person whose surname GPT-2 splits into a first piece and a continuation piece (e.g. ' Kal'+'ovich'), then mentions the person again and stops after the first piece. The clean and corrupted prompts differ only in the continuation piece of the first mention, so the next token must be copied from that earlier occurrence. good is the clean continuation, bad is the corrupted one.

roles.L4/N2999: marks word-internal pieces of rare, long or technical-looking words, which makes the earlier surname pieces readable as one rare word.
roles.L5/N1208: detects that the continuation piece extends a character-level run begun by the previous token, mostly from the previous token's identity; provides the previous-token feature at the earlier continuation piece that the induction key reads.
roles.L5/N2567: fires on the token that completes a locally predictable 2-3 token unit; marks the earlier continuation piece as the completion of the surname.
roles.L5/N616: fires on a non-initial subword that finishes a split word begun in the preceding 1-2 tokens; adds to the same word-completion signal at the earlier continuation piece.
roles.L6/N37: fires on the token that completes a conventional chunk cued by the preceding tokens; carries the completion signal into layer 7 where the heads read it.
roles.L7/H10: induction head; at the second mention's first piece it attends to the earlier continuation piece and writes it, strongest when the copied token is a piece of a word split into 2+ tokens, as here.
roles.L7/H2: induction head; matches the repeated span (title plus first piece) to its earlier copy and attends to and writes the token that followed it, adding to H10's copy of the continuation piece.

hypothesis.explanation: The circuit completes a rare multi-token word by copying it from its earlier occurrence in the context. At the first mention of a made-up surname, the L4-L6 neurons mark the continuation piece as the inside of a split word: L4/N2999 and L5/N1208 respond to the word-internal piece of an unusual word, and L5/N2567, L5/N616 and L6/N37 respond to the token that completes a multi-token unit started by the previous token. These signals give the continuation token a "previous token was the first piece of this word" representation that the induction heads can key on. At the second mention, which stops after the first piece, the L7 induction heads H10 and H2 match the current first piece to its earlier copy, attend to the continuation piece that followed it, and write that piece's identity toward the output. This raises the logit of the clean continuation (good) over the corrupted one (bad). The corrupted prompt changes only the earlier continuation piece, so the metric measures how much of the copied piece the circuit carries. L5/N1208: detects that the continuation piece extends a character-level run begun by the previous token, mostly from the previous token's identity; provides the previous-token feature at the earlier continuation piece that the induction key reads. L5/N2567: fires on the token that completes a locally predictable 2-3 token unit; marks the earlier continuation piece as the completion of the surname. L5/N616: fires on a non-initial subword that finishes a split word begun in the preceding 1-2 tokens; adds to the same word-completion signal at the earlier continuation piece. L6/N37: fires on the token that completes a conventional chunk cued by the preceding tokens; carries the completion signal into layer 7 where the heads read it.
